 WATCH: UCLA CB Scooter Jackson, guard Carter Sweazie look back on 9-0 start
 Tracy McDannald @ Tracy_McDannald 2h 0 Share Share 
 UCLA offensive guard Carter Sweazie has watched head coach Bob Chesney produce instant results before, while cornerback Scooter Jackson is in the midst of experiencing one of the country’s more remarkable turnarounds.

 Sweazie followed Chesney from James Madison, where they won a Sun Belt championship and reached the school’s first-ever College Football Playoff last season.
 Sweazie said the team’s unwavering belief in Chesney and the staff, regardless of a particular game’s circumstances, comes from “being tested in fire in practice every day.”
 “Reps build confidence,” Sweazie said at Monday’s press conference.
 Jackson decided to stick it out on Westwood after a three-win season that cost ex-head coach DeShaun Foster his job after an 0-3 start to his second year and paved the way for Chesney’s hire.
 Now, the 9-0 Bruins are a win shy of tying the single-season program record achieved on nine previous occasions, but not since 2014. Jackson said he is not paying attention to any benchmarks, but the difference in less than a calendar year is hard to ignore.
 “The culture is different,” Jackson said. “This has been the most exciting season that I’ve been a part of in college football. It’s just seeing different things. Coach Chesney has shown me a different way of how to play football, how to prepare — how to win.
 “It’s hard to explain. You guys see it. Everything that you guys see in the media, that’s him in real life.”
